words.gloss: altered, abnormal (vikṛta); disease (vyādhi); concerning knowledge, to be known (vijñānīya)

hindi: अब इसलिए हम विकृत व्याधियों के ज्ञान से सम्बन्धित अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter on the knowledge of abnormal (vikṛta) diseases.
notes: Opening formula (atha ataḥ ... vyākhyāsyāmaḥ). 'Vikṛtavyādhivijñānīya' is the chapter title; 'vikṛta' is rendered literally ('altered, abnormal'). The content of the chapter (signs of fatal disease) is not stated in this line and is not imported. Printed -yamadhyāyaṃ is simply -yam adhyāyam run together.

words.gloss: piplu (mole; probable); vyaṅga (blemish, a dark patch of the skin; probable); line (lekhā); tilakālaka (black specks on the skin; probable)
of one who is wasting away
eyelid (vartman); nose (nāsikā); either of the two (anyatara); swelling (śvayathu)
throat; mouth; anus; inflammation, literally ripening (pāka)
āmāśaya and pakvāśaya (the receptacles of raw and of cooked food; probably the stomach and the large intestine); one of the two (anyatara)

hindi: जिसकी व्याधि सब हेतुओं, पूर्वरूपों और रूपों के साथ, अपने-अपने अनुसार, अत्यधिक मात्रा में उत्पन्न होती है; या जिस रोगी के मुख पर शीघ्र पिप्लु यानी सम्भवतः मस्से, व्यंग यानी सम्भवतः त्वचा के काले धब्बे, रेखाएँ और तिलकालक यानी सम्भवतः त्वचा के काले कण हैं, या नाखूनों और दाँतों पर पुष्प यानी फूल हैं, या पेट पर अनेक रंगों की सिराएँ यानी नसें हैं; जिसके सूखते हुए आँखों पर उपदेह यानी लेप है, पलक या नाक में से किसी एक की सूजन है, या पलक का झड़ना है; जिस क्षीण की भूख या प्यास बहुत से मनोहर अन्न और पेयों से भी शान्त नहीं होती; जिसका झाग सहित रक्त बहता है, कुक्षि यानी पेट के पार्श्व में शूल यानी पीड़ा और छाती की; या जिसका श्लेष्मा नीला, पीला और लाल है और बार-बार; जिसकी गर्दन का प्रबल अवमर्द यानी कुचला जाना, जीभ का सूखना, और कण्ठ, मुख तथा गुदा का पाक यानी पकना है; जिसके आमाशय यानी सम्भवतः जठर से उठी हुई परिकर्तिका यानी काटने वाली पीड़ा, अत्यन्त प्यास और मल का टूटना है; जिसके पक्वाशय यानी सम्भवतः बड़ी आँत से उठी हुई परिकर्तिका, अत्यन्त प्यास और अत्यधिक गुदग्रह यानी गुदा की जकड़न है; जिसके आमाशय या पक्वाशय में से किसी एक का आश्रय लेकर और संज्ञा यानी चेतना को नष्ट करके वायु कण्ठ में घुरघुरक यानी घुरघुर की आवाज़ करता है; जिस क्षीण की प्यास की वृद्धि और हृदय में शूल है, तथा हिचकी और रक्तातिसार यानी खूनी दस्त, या आध्मान यानी अफारा और अतिसार है, और जो बहुत प्यासा है, वह परासु है, यानी जिसके प्राण चले गए हैं।
english: He whose disease arises with all its causes, premonitory signs (prāgrūpa) and signs (rūpa), each in its own way, to excess; or a sick man in whom quickly there are, on the face, moles (piplu, probably), blemishes (vyaṅga, probably), lines (lekhā) and tilakālaka (black specks of the skin, probably), or, on the nails and teeth, flowers (puṣpa), or, on the belly, veins (sirā) of various colours; he who, while wasting away, has a coating on the eyes (netra-upadeha), a swelling of either the eyelid or the nose, or a drooping of the eyelid; he who, being wasted, has hunger or thirst that is not allayed even by many agreeable foods and drinks; he from whom frothy blood is discharged, with pain in the flank and (pain) of the chest; or he whose phlegm (śleṣman) is blue, yellow and red, and repeatedly so; he who has a strong crushing of the neck, dryness of the tongue, and inflammation (pāka, literally 'ripening') of the throat, mouth and anus; he who has parikartikā (cutting pain) arising in the āmāśaya (probably the stomach), excessive thirst and breaking of the stool; he who has parikartikā arising in the pakvāśaya (probably the large intestine), excessive thirst and an excessive grasp of the anus (gudagraha); he in whom wind (vāyu), having resorted to either the āmāśaya or the pakvāśaya and having destroyed consciousness (saṃjñā), makes a gurgling sound (ghurghuraka) in the throat; he who, wasted, has increase of thirst and pain in the heart, and likewise hiccup and bloody diarrhoea, or bloating and diarrhoea, and who is greatly thirsty: he is parāsu (one whose life-breaths are gone).

text_flags.why: possible: 'savair' is not a word; the r of 'sarvaiḥ' has dropped
possible: 'kṣaṇisya' is not a word; 'kṣīṇasya' (of the wasted one) matches the same phrase earlier in the unit
possible: printed 'satṛṣṇo sa' has o before s, which is not regular sandhi; satṛṣṇaḥ saḥ (thirsty, he) is meant

notes: One long prose sentence of alternative signs, each introduced by 'yasya' ('of whom/whose'); the closing 'sa parāsuḥ iti' gives the conclusion for each. Copula understood in the verbless clauses (shown as 'has' or 'there are'). The closing 'iti' is not translated. 'parāsu' = one whose life-breaths (asu) have gone; the line itself does not say 'doomed to die', so no more is added (the chapter appears to list fatal signs, but that is not stated here). Printed 'vāyasyāśu' = vā yasya āśu; 'cauraso' = ca urasaḥ (hiatus printed joined; 'śūla' of the chest is understood from kukṣiśūlam). 'puṣpa' = flowers, read literally; later medicine uses it for white spots on the nails (not adopted). tilakālaka, piplu and vyaṅga are skin marks (probable identifications). 'bahuśaḥ' is read as 'repeatedly'. 'netropadeha' = coating (smearing) on the eyes. 'śakṛdbheda' = breaking of the stool (probably loose stool). 'gudagraha' = grasp of the anus. 'āmapakvāśayānyataram' is read as 'one of the two, āmāśaya or pakvāśaya'. 'hidhmā-raktātisārau' and 'ādhmāna-atīsārau' are dual dvandvas (two members each). The avagraha printed after -ā (parikartikā'ti-) is a print habit. 'kṣaṇisya' is read as kṣīṇasya (flagged). Reviewer: ghurghuraka (a gurgling or rattling sound in the throat) is probably what is now called the death rattle (probable). The hiatus 'ca uraso' (Devanagari चउरसो) is the print's own spelling, not a typo.
lines_deva: सवैर्यथास्वं हेतुप्राग्रूपरूपैरतिमात्रैर्यस्य व्याधिरुत्पद्यते व्याधितस्य वायस्याशु मुखे पिप्लुव्यंगलेखातिलकालकाः करजरदनेषु वा पुष्पाण्युदरे वा नानावर्णाः सिराः यस्य शुष्यतो नेत्रोपदेहो वर्त्मनासिकान्यतरश्वयथुर्वर्त्मस्रंसो वा यस्य क्षीणस्य क्षुत्तृष्णा वा हृद्यैर्बहुभिरप्यन्नपानैर्न शाम्यति यस्य सफेनमसृक् प्रसिच्यते कुक्षिशूलं चउरसो वा यस्य श्लेष्मा नीलपीतलोहितो बहुशश्च यस्य बलवान् ग्रीवावमर्दो जिह्वाशोषः कंठास्यगुदपाकश्च यस्यामाशयोत्था परिकर्तिकाऽतितृष्णा शकृद्भेदश्च यस्य पक्वाशयोत्था परिकर्तिकाऽतितृष्णाऽतिमात्रश्च गुदग्रहः यस्यामपक्वाशयान्यतरमाश्रित्य संज्ञां च हत्वा वायुः कंठे घुर्घुरकं करोति यस्य क्षणिस्य तृष्णाभिवृद्धिर्हृदि शूलं च तथा हिध्मारक्तातिसारौ वाऽध्मानातीसारौ वा भृशं सतृष्णो स परासुरिति
lines_iast: savairyathāsvaṃ hetuprāgrūparūpairatimātrairyasya vyādhirutpadyate vyādhitasya vāyasyāśu mukhe pipluvyaṃgalekhātilakālakāḥ karajaradaneṣu vā puṣpāṇyudare vā nānāvarṇāḥ sirāḥ yasya śuṣyato netropadeho vartmanāsikānyataraśvayathurvartmasraṃso vā yasya kṣīṇasya kṣuttṛṣṇā vā hṛdyairbahubhirapyannapānairna śāmyati yasya saphenamasṛk prasicyate kukṣiśūlaṃ cauraso vā yasya śleṣmā nīlapītalohito bahuśaśca yasya balavān grīvāvamardo jihvāśoṣaḥ kaṃṭhāsyagudapākaśca yasyāmāśayotthā parikartikā'titṛṣṇā śakṛdbhedaśca yasya pakvāśayotthā parikartikā'titṛṣṇā'timātraśca gudagrahaḥ yasyāmapakvāśayānyataramāśritya saṃjñāṃ ca hatvā vāyuḥ kaṃṭhe ghurghurakaṃ karoti yasya kṣaṇisya tṛṣṇābhivṛddhirhṛdi śūlaṃ ca tathā hidhmāraktātisārau vā'dhmānātīsārau vā bhṛśaṃ satṛṣṇo sa parāsuriti

hindi: और इस विषय में है:
english: And on this matter there is:
notes: Lead-in formula 'bhavati ca atra' ('and here there is ...'); nothing is supplied after it because the Sanskrit states no object. GROUPING: this unit is a formula that appears to introduce the verse units that follow (line 4 (card 4) onward).

words.gloss: destroyed (hata); fire (anala; probably the digestive fire)

hindi: बलवान्, गहरा और दीर्घरात्रिक यानी लम्बी रातों वाला ज्वर यानी बुखार मारता है। प्रलाप यानी बड़बड़ाहट, भ्रम यानी चक्कर और श्वास यानी साँस फूलने से युक्त; क्षीण, सूजे हुए, और जिसकी अग्नि यानी सम्भवतः पाचन की अग्नि नष्ट हो गई है उसको।
english: A fever (jvara) that is strong, deep (gambhīra) and long-lasting (dīrgharātrika, literally 'of long nights') kills. Accompanied by delirium (pralāpa), giddiness (bhrama) and breathlessness (śvāsa); the one who is wasted, swollen, whose fire (anala, probably the digestive fire) is destroyed.
notes: [02.11.4] The verb nihanti has no object in this line; accusative objects follow in the next units, so the sentence is left as the Sanskrit gives it. 'dīrgharātrika' is literally 'having long nights' (lasting many days). [02.11.5] The first word is nominative and agrees with jvaraḥ of line 4 (card 4); the other three words are accusative, the objects of nihanti in line 4 (card 4) (the verb is carried over, none is supplied). 'anala' = fire, probably the digestive fire (probable).

hindi: जो कृश नहीं है, जिसकी वाणी अटकती है, लाल आँखों वाले और हृदय में शूल यानी पीड़ा वाले को। संशुष्क कास यानी अत्यन्त सूखी खाँसी, जो पूर्वाह्न में या अपराह्न में भी हो।
english: The one who is not emaciated (akṣāma), whose speech is faltering (sakta-vacana, literally 'speech stuck'), who is red-eyed and has pain in the heart (hṛd). A very dry cough (saṃśuṣka-kāsa) that may occur in the forenoon or even in the afternoon.

text_flags.why: possible: 'not emaciated' sits oddly beside kṣīṇam (wasted) in line 5 (card 4); 'kṣāmam' (emaciated, or of weak voice) may be meant. Not adopted: the printed word is a valid word and is translated as printed.

notes: [02.11.6] Accusative objects continue from line 4 (card 4)/5 (verb carried over). akṣāma is translated as printed ('not emaciated'); its fit beside 'kṣīṇam' is doubtful, hence the flag and medium confidence. sakta = clinging or stuck, so sakta-vacana is faltering or halting speech. [02.11.7] Fresh nominative subject; it is not said in this line what it does (the sentence is a list of ominous signs begun in line 4 (card 4)).

hindi: बल और मांस से रहित का, श्लेष्मकास यानी कफ की खाँसी से युक्त। रक्तपित्त यानी सम्भवतः रक्तस्राव का रोग, बहुत लाल, काला, इन्द्रधनुष की आभा वाला।
english: Of one deprived of strength and flesh, accompanied by phlegm-cough (śleṣma-kāsa). Raktapitta (a bleeding disorder, probably), very red, black, with the lustre of the rainbow (Indra's bow).

text_flags.why: 'idra' is not a word; the anusvāra of 'indra' has dropped (the sense 'rainbow' is certain)

notes: [02.11.8] GROUPING: appears to continue line 7 (card 5). Whether 'samanvitaḥ' (nominative) qualifies the dry cough of line 7 (card 5) or the person is not decided by the Sanskrit; both are shown literally. śleṣma-kāsa = cough with phlegm (Kapha cough). [02.11.9] raktapitta = disorder of bleeding from the body (probable); the term is kept. 'bhṛśam' is read with 'raktam' ('very red'); it could also be a separate adverb. The adjectives describe the discharged blood, which is not named in this line.

words.gloss: hair (roma); pit, pore (kūpa); spread forth, issued (pravisṛta)

hindi: ताँबे के रंग का, हल्दी के रंग का, हरा और लाल रूप दिखाए। रोमकूप यानी रोमछिद्रों से निकला हुआ; कण्ठ, मुख और हृदय में अस्पष्ट शब्द सजत, अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: It should show a copper-coloured, turmeric-coloured, green and red (rakta) appearance (rūpa). Issued through the hair-pits (roma-kūpa); an unclear word (printed sajataṃ) in the throat, mouth and heart (hṛdaya), on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: possible: 'sajata' is not a word as printed; 'saṃjātam' (arisen) or 'saktam' (clinging) are the nearest candidates. Neither is adopted; the word stays unclear.

notes: [02.11.10] 'raktam' is read as the colour 'red' in a list of colours; it could also be the noun 'blood' (so 'show blood in a copper-coloured, turmeric-coloured, green appearance'). The subject of darśayet is not stated (continuing raktapitta of line 9 (card 6); GROUPING: appears to continue line 9 (card 6)). [02.11.11] The printed word 'sajataṃ' is not restorable with certainty and is left unclear (candidates only in the flag). GROUPING: appears to continue lines 9-10 (card 6/7). 'pravisṛta' = spread forth, issued.

words.gloss: unclear (the stem chard- 'vomit' is visible but the form is doubtful)
pāṇḍu (anaemia with pallor; standard); fever (jvara); vomiting (chardi); cough (kāsa); swelling (śopha); having diarrhoea (atisārin)

hindi: वस्त्र का रंगना, सड़ा हुआ, वेग वाला और बहुत अधिक भी। अस्पष्ट शब्द छर्द्दं; पाण्डु यानी रक्ताल्पता, ज्वर, उल्टी, खाँसी, सूजन और अतिसार वाले को, अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: Staining of clothing; putrid (pūti), forceful and also very abundant. An unclear word (printed charddaṃ); the one who has pāṇḍu (anaemia with pallor), fever (jvara), vomiting (chardi), cough (kāsa), swelling (śopha) and diarrhoea (atisāra), on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.suggest: chardiṃ or another form of chard- (vomiting)
text_flags.why: possible: the form 'charddaṃ' is not clear and duplicates 'chardi' inside the next word; left unclear in the translation

notes: [02.11.12] Subject not stated; GROUPING: appears to continue lines 9-11 (card 6/7) (the discharge described there). 'pūti' is rendered 'putrid' (it may include foul smell). [02.11.13] Accusative object (verb carried over from line 4 (card 4)). Printed doubled 'dd' in chardi is a spelling habit and is written 'chardi' in the words. The first word is left unclear because its form is doubtful.

words.gloss: fever (jvara); vomiting (chardi); thirst (tṛṣṇā); diarrhoea (atīsāra); having swelling (śophin)
side (pārśva); pain (ruj); distension (ānāha); blood (rakta); vomiting (chardi); not (a); burning heat, distress (saṃtāpin)

hindi: खाँसी यानी कास और साँस फूलना यानी श्वास; ज्वर यानी बुखार, उल्टी, प्यास, अतिसार यानी दस्त और सूजन वाले को। यक्ष्मन् यानी सम्भवतः क्षय रोग; पार्श्व में पीड़ा, आनाह यानी पेट के तनाव, रक्त की उल्टी वाले और ताप से रहित को।
english: Cough and breathlessness (kāsa and śvāsa); the one with fever (jvara), vomiting (chardi), thirst (tṛṣṇā), diarrhoea (atīsāra) and swelling. Yakṣman (consumption, probably tuberculosis); the one with pain in the side, distension (ānāha), vomiting of blood, and without burning heat (asaṃtāpin).
notes: [02.11.14] Elliptical: nominative dual subject, accusative object, verb (nihanti) carried over from line 4 (card 4) and not supplied. Printed 'atīsāra' (long ī) is kept as printed. [02.11.15] Elliptical (verb carried over). The last element 'a-saṃtāpin' is read literally as 'without burning heat/distress'; its sense in a list of ominous signs is not clear, hence medium confidence. ānāha = distension.

words.gloss: with asra (sa-asra; asra = blood or tears)

hindi: उल्टी यानी छर्दि, वेगवती, मूत्र और मल की गन्ध वाली, चन्द्रिका सहित; चन्द्रिका यानी चाँदनी, जिसका यहाँ अर्थ अस्पष्ट है। अस्र यानी रक्त या आँसू से युक्त; अस्पष्ट समास विट्पूयरुक्कासश्वासवत्य; अस्पष्ट शब्द गुंषिणो; अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: Vomiting (chardi), forceful, smelling of urine and faeces, with candrikā (literally 'moonlight'; its sense here is uncertain). With asra (blood, or tears); an unclear compound (printed viṭpūyarukkāsaśvāsavatya); an unclear word (printed guṃṣiṇo); on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: possible: 'guṃṣiṇo' is not a word; 'yakṣmiṇaḥ' (of consumptives) is a conceivable but unproven correction. Not adopted.
possible: the ending '-vatya' does not parse; the compound is left unsplit and untranslated

notes: [02.11.16] 'candrikā' is literally moonlight (or moon-like marks); what it names here is not stated, so no interpretation is added. Printed doubled 'dd' in chardi normalised. Reviewer: candrikā might name moon-like (peacock-eye) marks in the discharge; possible, unverified, not adopted. [02.11.17] Damaged print. Visible parts of the long compound are viṭ (faeces), pūya (pus), ruj (pain), kāsa (cough), śvāsa (breath), but the ending is not clear, so it is not translated in part. 'sāsra' is read as sa-asra; asra can mean blood or tear. GROUPING: appears to continue the list of line 15-16 (card 9/10) (yakṣman), not certain.

words.gloss: madātyaya (ailment from intoxicating drink, an alcohol-related disorder; probable)

hindi: तृष्णा यानी प्यास; दूसरे रोगों से क्षीण किए गए, बाहर निकली जीभ वाले और अचेत को। मदात्यय यानी सम्भवतः मद्य से उत्पन्न रोग; अत्यन्त शीत से पीड़ित, क्षीण और तेल की चमक वाले मुख वाले को।
english: Thirst (tṛṣṇā); the one worn down by other ailments, with the tongue outside, unconscious. Madātyaya (an ailment from intoxicating drink, probably an alcohol-related disorder); the one afflicted by great cold, wasted, whose face has the lustre of oil.
notes: [02.11.18] Elliptical (verb carried over). The avagraha printed after -ā (tṛṣṇā'nya-) is a print habit. 'bahir-jihva' = tongue outside (protruding). [02.11.19] Elliptical (verb carried over). The avagraha is printed (madātyayo 'ti-); regular sandhi for madātyayaḥ ati.

words.gloss: hand (pāṇi); foot (pad); navel (nābhi); anus (guda); testicle (muṣka); mouth (āsya); having swelling (śophin)
heart (hṛd); side (pārśva); limb, body part (aṅga); pain (rujā); vomiting (chardi); anus (pāyu); inflammation, literally ripening (pāka); fever (jvara); afflicted (ātura)

hindi: अर्श यानी बवासीर; हाथ, पैर, नाभि, गुदा, मुष्क यानी वृषण और मुख में सूजन वाले को। हृदय, पार्श्व और अंग की पीड़ा, उल्टी, गुदा के पाक यानी पकने और ज्वर से पीड़ित को।
english: Arśas (haemorrhoids, piles); the one with swelling of the hands, feet, navel, anus, testicles (muṣka) and mouth. The one afflicted by pain in the heart, side and limbs, vomiting, inflammation (pāka, literally 'ripening') of the anus, and fever.

text_flags.why: anusvāra dropped: the neuter plural of arśas is arśāṃsi
possible: pārśva + aṅga should give pārśvāṅga (long ā); the print has short a ('pārśvaṃga'); ṅ printed as ṃ is the print's habit. Read as pārśva-aṅga in `words`; the sense is unchanged.

notes: [02.11.20] Elliptical (verb carried over). 'pannābhi' is pad + nābhi (regular sandhi). āsya = mouth (also 'face'). [02.11.21] Elliptical (verb carried over; GROUPING: line 21 (card 12) appears to complete the object begun in line 20 (card 12), arśas). The compound can also be read as 'pain of heart, side and limb' in one group, as here.

words.gloss: liver (yakṛt); lump (piṇḍa); flesh, meat (māṃsa); washing (dhāvana); dark blue-black (mecaka)
oil (taila); ghee (ghṛta); milk (kṣīra); curd (dadhi); marrow (majjā); fat (vasā); fermented liquor (āsava)

hindi: अतिसार यानी दस्त, यकृत के पिण्डों, मांस के धोवन और गहरे नीले-काले से। तेल, घी, दूध, दही, मज्जा, वसा यानी मांस की चर्बी और आसव यानी किण्वित पेय के समान।
english: Diarrhoea (atīsāra), with liver-lumps (yakṛt-piṇḍa), meat-washings (māṃsa-dhāvana) and dark (mecaka) ones. Similar to oil, ghee, milk, curd, marrow, fat (vasā) and āsava (a fermented liquor).
notes: [02.11.22] The instrumental plurals may be completed by 'tulyaḥ' in line 23 (card 13) (similar to), in which case 'with' here would read 'like'; the construction is left as printed (open). 'mecaka' = dark blue-black (also peacock-coloured); read as an adjective with an unstated noun, shown as '(ones)'. GROUPING: appears to continue in line 23-24 (card 13/14). [02.11.23] Continues line 22 (card 13) (diarrhoea). 'majja' in a compound is the stem of majjā or majjan; 'marrow' in this body context. GROUPING: appears to continue line 22 (card 13) and run on into line 24 (card 14).

words.gloss: first part of mastuluṅga (brain-matter; probable), printed apart from luṅga
second part of mastuluṅga; soot (maṣī); pus (pūya); veśavāra (a preparation of minced meat; standard); water (ambu); honey (mākṣika)
red (rakta); black (asita); unctuous (snigdha); putrid (pūti); clear (accha); thick, dense (ghana); pain, feeling (vedana)

hindi: मस्तुलुंग यानी सम्भवतः मस्तिष्क का पदार्थ, मषी यानी कालिख, पूय यानी मवाद, वेशवार यानी पिसे हुए मांस की बनी तैयारी, जल और शहद से, अनुमानित पाठ पर। अति लाल, काला, चिकना, सड़ा हुआ, स्वच्छ, घना, पीड़ा वाला।
english: With mastuluṅga (brain-matter, probably), soot (maṣī), pus (pūya), veśavāra (a preparation of minced meat), water and honey, on a conjectural reading. Very (ati) red, black, unctuous (snigdha), putrid (pūti), clear (accha), thick (ghana), with pain (vedana).

text_flags.why: possible: a space has fallen inside the word 'mastuluṅga' (brain). Alternative: mastu (whey) and luṅga (citron) as two words. The joined reading is adopted and marked conjectural in the translations.
possible: 'raṃbu' has a stray anusvāra for 'rāmbu' (veśavāra + ambu); 'vesavāra' is spelled with s for ś

notes: [02.11.24] Continues the list of lines 22-23 (card 13). The word-space in 'mastu luṃga' is read as an error for mastuluṅga (brain), which is a conjecture; hence the conjectural mark. 'veśavāra' = a preparation of boneless minced meat (standard, name kept). [02.11.25] 'ati' is printed apart and is kept as a separate adverb; it could also be the first member of a compound with 'rakta'. The noun described is not stated (the stool, continuing lines 22-24 (card 13/14), appears likely). 'ghana-vedana' could also be 'with dense (intense) pain'.

hindi: चितकबरा; अस्पष्ट शब्द प्रस्रवन्धात्त्रिष्पूरीषो; अथवा बहुत अधिक मल वाला; अनुमानित पाठ पर। तन्तुओं वाला, मषिका यानी कालिख के कण से आक्रान्त, अस्पष्ट शब्द राजैर्मांसेंद्रकैर् से युक्त; अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: Mottled (karbura); an unclear word (printed prasravandhāttriṣpūrīṣo); or else with excessive faeces (ati-viṭ); on a conjectural reading. Fibrous (tantumat), overspread (ākrānta) with soot-specks (maṣikā), joined with unclear words (printed rājair māṃseṃdrakair); on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: possible: 'dhāttriṣ' does not parse; 'triṣ' may be 'niṣ' (nasal/tra confusion), giving niṣpūrīṣaḥ (without faeces), which would pair with 'ati-viṭ' (with much faeces). Not adopted; left unclear.
possible: s for ṣ (the print confuses these elsewhere)
possible: 'rājair' and 'māṃseṃdrakair' do not give a sure sense; left unclear

notes: [02.11.26] Damaged print. The visible word 'prasravan' (flowing) is joined to the unclear part by sandhi, so the whole stretch is left unsplit and unclear. The avagraha after -ā in 'athavā'ti-' is a print habit. [02.11.27] Continues the description of the stool (lines 22-26 (card 13/15)). 'maṣikā' is read as soot or black specks; the s/ṣ spelling is a print habit. The last two words are not restorable and are left unclear.

hindi: शीर्ण गुदा की वलि यानी तह वाले, मुक्त नाल यानी छूटे हुए डंठल वाले और जोड़ों व हड्डियों में शूल यानी पीड़ा वाले को, अनुमानित पाठ पर। गुदा के खिसकने यानी सम्भवतः निकल आने वाले, बल से क्षीण को; अस्पष्ट शब्द अन्नेवोपवेशयन्; अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: The one whose folds (vali) of the anus are withered, whose stalk (nāla) is released (its sense here is uncertain), who has pain in the joints and bones; on a conjectural reading. The one with a slipped anus (srasta-pāyu, probably prolapse of the anus or rectum), wasted in strength; an unclear word (printed annevopaveśayan); on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: possible: 'vāli' (long ā) may be 'vali' (fold); the print interchanges v and b elsewhere and vowel lengths are loose. Adopted conjecturally.

text_flags.suggest: annaṃ vā upaveśayan or anne vā upaveśayan
text_flags.why: possible: both parse as 'anna(m) vā upaveśayan' but the sense of upaveśayan ('causing to sit') is not clear here. Left unclear.

notes: [02.11.28] Elliptical (verb carried over). 'nāla' = stalk; what is meant (perhaps a part of the anus or rectum) is not stated, so nothing is added. [02.11.29] The last word is left unclear. srasta-pāyu = slipped anus (prolapse of the anus or rectum, probable). GROUPING: appears to continue the object list of lines 26-28 (card 15/16).

words.gloss: fever (jvara); vomiting (chardi); burning (dāha); distension (ānāha); having pravāhikā (flux with straining, dysentery; probable)

hindi: प्यास सहित, खाँसी, ज्वर, उल्टी, दाह यानी जलन, आनाह यानी पेट के तनाव और प्रवाहिका यानी सम्भवतः मरोड़ के साथ पेचिश वाला; अनुमानित पाठ पर। अश्मरी यानी मूत्र की पथरी; सूजे हुए वृषणों वाले, रुके हुए मूत्र वाले और पीड़ा से पीड़ित को।
english: With thirst, cough, fever, vomiting, burning (dāha), distension (ānāha) and pravāhikā (flux with straining, probably dysentery); on a conjectural reading. Aśmarī (urinary stone); the one with swollen testicles, with obstructed urine, afflicted by pain.

text_flags.suggest: satṛṭ kāsa (and the next token then begins jvara-)
text_flags.why: possible: 'satṛṭkā majvara-' does not parse; 'sa' and 'ma' are confused in this print, so the next word likely begins 'jvara' and 'kāsa' (cough) is meant. Syllable count (16) is the same either way. Adopted conjecturally.

notes: [02.11.30] Nominative adjectives for the stool/diarrhoea of lines 22-29 (card 13/16). The emendation moves a letter across the token boundary, so the tokens are given as printed and the words as emended. pravāhikā is flux with straining (probable). [02.11.31] Elliptical (verb carried over from line 4 (card 4)).

words.gloss: meha (prameha, a urinary disorder, probably the diabetes-type; probable)
pricking pain (tud); burning (dāha); boils (piṭakā); flesh (māṃsa); decay (kotha); having diarrhoea (atisārin)
vital spot (marma); heart (hṛd); back (pṛṣṭha); breast (stana); shoulder (aṃsa); anus (guda); head (mūrdhan); situated in (-ga)

hindi: मेह यानी प्रमेह, सम्भवतः मधुमेह वाला रूप; चुभने वाली पीड़ा, दाह यानी जलन, पिटिका यानी फुंसियों, मांस के सड़ने और अतिसार यानी दस्त वाले को। पिटिकाएँ यानी फुंसियाँ, मर्म, हृदय, पीठ, स्तन, कन्धे, गुदा और सिर में स्थित, अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: Meha (prameha, a urinary disorder, probably the diabetes-type); the one with pricking pain (tud), burning, boils (piṭakā), decay of flesh and diarrhoea. Boils (piṭikā) situated in the vital spots (marma), heart, back, breast, shoulder, anus and head; on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: possible: 'tuddvāha' has a stray v; 'tud-dāha' (pricking pain, burning) is meant
possible: 'hat' for 'hṛt' (heart); the ṛ-sign is dropped. Adopted conjecturally.

notes: [02.11.32] Elliptical (verb carried over). meha is the general urinary disorder, here read as prameha, probably the diabetes-type (probable). Printed 'dd' in tuddāha: tud + dāha. Reviewer: 'tud' alone is not an attested noun for pricking pain (toda/tuda would be). Alternative to the flagged tud-dāha: tṛḍ-dāha (thirst, burning), possible, not adopted; if either is adopted the translations need the conjectural mark. [02.11.33] The final visarga of piṭikāḥ is regular sandhi before m. GROUPING: appears to continue in line 34 (card 19) ('or situated in the joints, feet or hands'). marma is a doctrinal term and is kept.

words.gloss: having prameha (prameha, a urinary disorder; probable)
flesh (māṃsa); decay (saṃkotha); burning (dāha); thirst (tṛṣṇā); intoxication (mada); fever (jvara)

hindi: जोड़ों, पैरों या हाथों में स्थित; मन्द उत्साह वाले और प्रमेह यानी मूत्र के रोग वाले को। और सब, मांस के सड़ने, दाह यानी जलन, प्यास, मद यानी नशा और ज्वर से।
english: (Boils) situated in the joints, feet or hands; the one of low energy (manda-utsāha) who has prameha (a urinary disorder). And all, with decay of flesh (māṃsa-saṃkotha), burning (dāha), thirst (tṛṣṇā), intoxication (mada) and fever (jvara).

text_flags.why: possible: final anusvāra dropped in 'pramehiṇa'; an accusative is expected like the neighbouring objects

notes: [02.11.34] Continues line 33 (card 18). The 'or' (vā) follows the place compound and is read as distributive. The unstated noun 'boils' is shown in brackets in English only. [02.11.35] Continues lines 32-34 (card 18/19). 'sarvam' ('all') is left as printed; what it refers to is not stated. GROUPING: appears to continue line 34 (card 19).

words.gloss: visarpa (erysipelas, a spreading skin inflammation; probable); vital spot (marma); obstruction (saṃrodha); hiccup (hidhmā); breathlessness (śvāsa); giddiness (bhrama); fatigue (klama)
gulma (an abdominal lump or swelling; probable)

hindi: विसर्प यानी सम्भवतः त्वचा का फैलने वाला शोथ, मर्म के संरोध यानी रुकावट, हिचकी, श्वास यानी साँस फूलना, चक्कर और थकावट से। गुल्म यानी सम्भवतः पेट की गाँठ, चौड़े घेरे वाला, घना, कछुए के समान ऊँचा उठा हुआ।
english: With visarpa (erysipelas, a spreading skin inflammation, probably), obstruction of the vital spots (marma-saṃrodha), hiccup (hidhmā), breathlessness (śvāsa), giddiness (bhrama) and fatigue (klama). Gulma (an abdominal lump, probably), broad in girth, dense (ghana), raised like a tortoise.
notes: [02.11.36] Continues line 35 (card 19) (instrumental list). marma-saṃrodha is read as 'obstruction of the marmas'; marma is kept as a doctrinal term. [02.11.37] A fresh subject (gulma) described by adjectives; the verb is not stated. The Devanagari prints कूर्मइवोन्नतः, i.e. kūrma iva unnataḥ with a hiatus (kūrmaḥ + iva, regular); the IAST kūrmaiva is an intake artefact, not a typo.

words.gloss: fever (jvara); vomiting (chardi); hiccup (hidhmā); bloating (ādhmāna); pain (ruj); accompanied (anvita)
cough (kāsa); pīnasa (chronic nasal catarrh; probable); nausea (hṛllāsa); breathlessness (śvāsa); diarrhoea (atīsāra); swelling (śopha); having (-vat)

hindi: सिराओं यानी नसों से बँधा हुआ, ज्वर, उल्टी, हिचकी, आध्मान यानी अफारा और पीड़ा से युक्त। खाँसी, पीनस यानी सम्भवतः पुराना जुकाम, हृल्लास यानी मिचली, श्वास यानी साँस फूलना, अतिसार यानी दस्त और सूजन वाला।
english: Bound by sirās (veins), accompanied by fever, vomiting, hiccup, bloating (ādhmāna) and pain. Having cough, pīnasa (chronic nasal catarrh, probably), nausea (hṛllāsa), breathlessness, diarrhoea (atīsāra) and swelling.
notes: [02.11.38] Continues the description of the gulma of line 37 (card 20) (nominative). The avagraha after -ā (hidhmā'dhmāna) is a print habit. sirā = vein or vessel (probable). [02.11.39] Nominative continuing lines 37-38 (card 20/21) (the gulma).

words.gloss: faeces (viṭ); urine (mūtra); retention (saṃgraha); breathlessness (śvāsa); swelling (śopha); hiccup (hidhmā); fever (jvara); giddiness (bhrama)
jaṭhara (belly; here probably the belly disorder, an ascites-type; probable)

hindi: मल और मूत्र के संग्रह यानी रुकने, श्वास यानी साँस फूलने, सूजन, हिचकी, ज्वर और चक्कर से। और मूर्च्छा यानी बेहोशी, उल्टी तथा अतिसार यानी दस्त के साथ जठर यानी पेट, यहाँ सम्भवतः पेट का रोग, जलोदर प्रकार का, दुर्बल को मारता है।
english: With retention (saṃgraha) of faeces and urine, breathlessness, swelling, hiccup, fever and giddiness. And with fainting (mūrcchā), vomiting and diarrhoea, jaṭhara (belly; here probably the belly disorder, an ascites-type) kills the weak (one).
notes: [02.11.40] Instrumental list continuing 38-39. GROUPING: appears to continue into line 41 (card 22) ('jaṭharam ... hanti'). [02.11.41] Here the verb hanti ('kills') is stated, matching nihanti of line 4 (card 4). 'jaṭhara' is the belly; read as the disease of the belly in this list of fatal conditions (probable). 'durbalam' is shown as 'the weak (one)'. GROUPING: appears to complete the sentence run of lines 39-40 (card 21/22).

words.gloss: crooked, twisted; upastha (the genitals, private parts; standard)
purgation (virecana); struck, harmed (on a conjectural reading; printed hatānām)
being distended, bloated (ānāha: distension with obstruction)

hindi: सूजी आँखों वाले, टेढ़े उपस्थ यानी जननांग वाले और गीली पतली त्वचा वाले को। अनुमानित पाठ पर: विरेचन से आहत, बार-बार आनाह यानी रुकावट के साथ पेट फूलने से ग्रस्त होते हुए को।
english: (One) with swollen eyes, crooked genitals (upastha) and moist, thin skin. On a conjectural reading: (one) harmed by purgation (virecana) and distended (ānāha: bloating with retention) again and again.

text_flags.why: possible: 'hatānām' (genitive plural) cannot agree with the accusative singular 'ānahyantaṃ'; the sense (one harmed by purgation, bloated again and again) fits an accusative '-hataṃ'; whether a ca stood between is not known; also 'ānahyantaṃ' is an unusual parasmaipada participle (ānahyamānam expected)

notes: [02.11.42] GROUPING: appears to continue the description of the weak patient in line 41 (card 22) ('jaṭharaṃ haṃti durbalaṃ'); this unit has no verb and none is supplied. upastha = the private parts, genitals (standard). 'upaklinna-tanu-tvacam' is read as 'moist and thin skin'. [02.11.43] GROUPING: appears to continue 42. The first part of the printed token is doubtful; 'virecana-hatam' is an adopted conjecture, not a sure reading. 'ānāha' = bloating with retention of stool and wind. No verb in the unit.

words.gloss: pale (pāṇḍu); disease; pāṇḍuroga = pāṇḍu disease, anaemia with pallor (standard)
drowsiness (tandrā); burning (dāha); distaste for food (aruci); vomiting (chardi); fainting (mūrchā); flatulent distension (ādhmāna); diarrhoea (atisāra); having

hindi: सूजन वाला पाण्डु रोग यानी रक्ताल्पता; जिसमें पीली आँखें और नाखून दिखाई देते हैं, उसे। तन्द्रा यानी ऊँघ, दाह यानी जलन, अरुचि यानी भोजन में अरुचि, छर्दि यानी वमन, मूर्छा, आध्मान यानी पेट फूलना और अतिसार यानी दस्त वाला।
english: Pāṇḍu disease (pāṇḍuroga: anaemia with pallor) with swelling (śvayathu); (one) in whom yellow eyes and nails are seen. Having drowsiness (tandrā), burning (dāha), distaste for food (aruci), vomiting (chardi), fainting (mūrchā), flatulent distension (ādhmāna) and diarrhoea (atisāra).
notes: [02.11.44] GROUPING: lines 44-47 (card 24/25) appear to form one run of description, with the verb 'hanti' only in 47; no verb is supplied here. 'darśanam' is read as 'appearance, being seen'; 'pīta' is taken with both eyes and nails. [02.11.45] Continues the description of 44 (nominative). The avagraha printed after -ā (mūrcchā'dhmāna) is a print habit, not an elision. Orthography normalised in `w`: doubled consonants (ccharddi, mūrcchā) written chardi, mūrchā.

words.gloss: many; upadrava (complication, secondary affliction; standard); joined with
from the belly (kukṣi) and the private parts (guhya)

hindi: अनेक उपद्रवों यानी जटिलताओं से युक्त; दोनों पैरों से फैले हुए पुरुष को। सूजन स्त्री को मुख से मारती है; कुक्षि यानी पेट और गुह्य यानी गुप्त अंग से दोनों को भी मारती है।
english: Joined with many complications (upadrava); a man spread out from the two feet. Swelling (śopha) kills a woman from the face; from the belly and the private parts (guhya) it kills both as well.
notes: [02.11.46] 'prasṛtam' agrees with 'naram', but what has spread is not stated; 'śophaḥ' (swelling) in the next unit is the likely subject, but this is an inference. The dual 'pādābhyām' is ablative ('from') or instrumental ('by'); 'from' is taken. GROUPING: appears to continue 44-45 and lead to 47. [02.11.47] 'hanti' is repeated in the English and Hindi for the second half; it is stated once in the Sanskrit. 'ubhau' (both) most likely means man and woman (cf.
